s1.name: the launch screen

tester.identifier_found: none that names the place; the only words are the app's name and "This process may contain ads"
tester.deciding_evidence: no text other than the app's own name appears in any moment of the live launch screen; the splash exception applies to a disappearing-identifier transition, not to whether this screen names itself, and no scroll transition touches it. Low impact: transient, and it hands over by itself
tester.recommendation: label the progress indicator, e.g. "Starting PDF Reader..." or "Loading", so the screen says what it is

personas.expectation: I think the app is starting up, before I get to any real screen. I am guessing, because nothing says so.
personas.cue: The large app icon in the middle, the words "PDF Reader, PDF Viewer" under it, and the sentence "This process may contain ads". There is a grey track near the bottom with only a tiny dark sliver at its left end; I cannot be sure that is a progress bar.
personas.why: The only boxed text is the app's name. That tells me which app I opened, not where I am in it. Nothing says "Loading" or "Starting". The progress bar is almost empty, so it reads as a small mark, not as progress. "This process" does not say which process. There is also a grey placeholder block at the very bottom with a circle and bars that shows nothing I can name.
personas.solution: Put a literal word under the name, such as "Loading...", and make the progress bar visibly a bar from the first moment. Replace "This process" with what the process is, for example "Starting the app may show ads".

personas.expectation: I believe the application is starting up. I am at its front door, not yet anywhere inside it.
personas.cue: The large picture of a red document with a pencil, the words 'PDF Reader, PDF Viewer' in the middle, a grey bar near the bottom that seems to be filling, and the line 'This process may contain ads'.
personas.why: The only words that are large on the screen are the name of the application. That tells me which programme I have opened, but not what is happening. Nothing says 'starting' or 'please wait'. I am inferring it from the bar at the bottom, and I would not trust myself to remember that inference if I looked away. The word 'process' in 'This process may contain ads' does not tell me which process.
personas.solution: A plain sentence under the name, such as 'Opening PDF Reader, please wait', so that I know I have not yet arrived anywhere and need do nothing.

personas.expectation: I think I am at the very start: the app is opening and has not reached any real page yet.
personas.cue: The large logo in the middle, the words "PDF Reader, PDF Viewer" under it, and a thin bar near the bottom that looks like it is filling up. The line "This process may contain ads" also suggests something is running.
personas.why: The only name on the screen is the app's own name, which tells me which app I have opened but not which part of it I am in. Nothing says "Loading" or "Starting", so I have to infer from the bar and the empty space. The word "process" is vague to me: which process? I read that line several times. I am fairly confident of my interpretation, but only after working it out.
personas.solution: Put one plain word with the bar, such as "Loading, please wait", so I do not have to deduce it. Say what "this process" is.

personas.expectation: I'm at the very start - the app is opening and loading.
personas.cue: The big red PDF logo with 'PDF Reader, PDF Viewer' under it, and the loading bar near the bottom that's only just started.
personas.why: It's a start-up screen and it looks like one - logo, name, loading bar, nothing else to decide. The name is only the app's name, but on a loading screen that's all I need. Honestly my eye went more to 'This process may contain ads' and the empty grey strip at the very bottom, because it makes me brace for an ad popping in - that's not about knowing where I am, though.
